outline.rationale: The user is a complete database beginner whose explicit goal is backing an app, so the outline starts with the conceptual foundation (relational model) since they can't design schemas without it, then moves through the practical shipping path: setup/connection, schema design, relationships (broken out separately because foreign keys are the single hardest concept for beginners and deserve their own node), the CRUD queries an app actually issues, data integrity (constraints + transactions, both app-correctness concerns), wiring Postgres into application code (their stated end goal), and finally migrations since any real app's schema evolves. I deliberately excluded administration, replication, indexing/performance tuning, internals, and analytics per the confirmed understanding, keeping depth at confident-beginner level. Nodes are MECE: concepts, environment, design, relationships, querying, integrity, app integration, and schema evolution each cover distinct content with minimal overlap.
